speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) for each year from 2019 to 2024, how many cases has the Ministry received from creators seeking help about the plagiarising of their artworks; (b) how many cases have been satisfactorily resolved and what are the remedies; (c) what steps are taken to ensure that businesses know of the need to engage the creators on using their intellectual property (IP); and (d) what avenues are available to creators to get affordable help to enforce their IP rights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This includes understanding available options if they find that their rights have potentially been infringed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Due to the confidential nature of these sessions, IPOS is not privy to the details of individual cases, including their progress and outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: IPOS also provides a variety of initiatives to increase public awareness of IP rights and build up IP capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, IPOS’ subsidiary IPOS International runs the IP Academy, which conducts courses to raise the understanding of IP amongst businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The MOU builds on collaborations between IPOS and VICPA since 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Working with VICPA and other partners continues to be an important approach to supporting creators across the multi-faceted issues that they face.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: For creators with less means, in terms of financial means, what is the assistance that they can look towards the Ministry or IPOS to provide.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: When this happens, what are the steps the Ministry can take to assist local creators to enforce such rights?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: That is something that is also available to those who own creative rights.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: I would just like to put across a point that while the creators can get some level of assistance and education, then I think the request to the Ministry is whether it can consider also mounting similar education for businesses, especially as such artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools become more popular and to educate businesses on how to seek IP rights from creators.
